markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests Normal (64%)** · Unreliable input · Careful review
Reliability check flagged this read and the second model disagrees; invasive probability rounds to 0% [F1].

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | Normal 64%, Benign 36% | Close two-way split |
| Conformal set | Normal, Benign (90%) | Two classes not separable |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.38 / 46th percentile | Flagged low; image typical |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | No | Disagrees on top class |
| Similar cases | 2 of 5 Normal [F5] | Mixed; three are Benign |

## Tissue evidence
- **Normal lobules** (regions 6, 9, 10) · ↓ invasive · Strongest association with lower invasive likelihood [F2] · Unreliable (spot check 0/20)
- **Tumor infiltrating stroma** (region 7) · ↑ invasive · Only invasive-leaning concept; single region [F3] · Validated
- **Benign fibrous stroma or fat** (region 6) · ↓ invasive · Associated with non-invasive tissue · Validated
- **Immune cell fraction** (regions 7, 8, 11) · context · 11% of nuclei, 93rd percentile; sampled regions only [F7] · Measured

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing the top 3 regions drops the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60); faithful to the classifier.
- **Concepts**: Deletion CI (−0.005 to 0.007) includes 0: not shown to reflect the classifier. Normal lobules is Unreliable.

## Could be wrong if
- Reliability is low (0.38), so the Normal-versus-Benign split may be unstable.
- The cell sample is thin: too few tumor nuclei in regions 7, 8, 11.

## Check on the slide
1. **Region 7:** Confirm true stromal infiltration; it is the only invasive-leaning region.
2. **Regions 6, 9, 10:** Verify normal two-layered lobules; the concept's spot check failed.
3. **Regions 7, 8, 11:** Look for neoplastic nuclei behind the high inflammatory-cell fraction.
